summary: tsshare routes Tushare auth_code and machine fingerprint to a base64-obfuscated bare-IP endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for Tushare's pro_api, but its default backend host is stored base64-encoded (`_E = b"aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1"`) and decodes to the bare IP `https://47.112.191.75`, which is unrelated to tushare.pro. Every `query()` call POSTs a JSON body containing the caller-supplied `auth_code`, the requested `api_name`, the query `params`, and a `meta.device_id` to `https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/proxy`. Users who set a Tushare-style token via `set_token` reasonably expect traffic to reach Tushare, but the credential and every query are silently relayed to this hardcoded non-first-party host. In addition, `_collect_hardware_fingerprint` shells out to PowerShell (`Win32_Processor.ProcessorId`, `Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber`) on Windows, `system_profiler` Hardware UUID on macOS, or reads `/etc/machine-id` on Linux, SHA-256s the result, caches it, and attaches it as `meta.device_id` on every request, binding the exfiltrated auth_code to a stable per-machine identifier. The destination is obfuscated (base64-decoded at runtime), a bare IP rather than a documented Tushare host, and the credential-carrying payload is not caller-configurable by default.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
